inputs.original_text: Local organizers in southern Alberta are gathering signatures for the Water Not Coal petition that Corb Lund launched last month. This citizen initiative is calling on the Government of Alberta to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” This is being spun as a necessary grassroots effort to challenge big business, but it really represents an attempt by progressive forces to impose restrictions that would damage Alberta's traditional industries. These industries have provided stable employment and supported family values through generations of hard work and resource stewardship. Instead of allowing such petitions to dictate policy, we should uphold the authority of the provincial government to pursue balanced development that strengthens our nation and prioritizes the well-being of ordinary citizens over radical environmental demands.
inputs.modified_text: Folks in southern Alberta are out gathering signatures for that Water Not Coal petition Corb Lund launched last month. The thing demands the Government of Alberta prohibit through legislation all coal exploration. This gets dressed up as some ordinary citizens taking on big business, but anyone paying attention can see it's really progressive forces trying to handcuff Alberta's traditional industries. Those industries have delivered steady work and upheld family values across generations through hard work and responsible resource use. We ought to reject letting these petitions run the show and instead back the authority of the provincial government to deliver balanced development that strengthens our nation while putting the well-being of regular citizens ahead of radical environmental demands.
